{{Short description|Russian mathematician (1929–2000)}}
'''Alexei Ivanovich Kostrikin''' ({{langx|ru|Алексей Иванович Кострикин}}) (12 February 1929&nbsp;– 22 September 2000) was a [[Russia|Russian]] [[mathematician]], specializing in [[abstract algebra|algebra]] and [[algebraic geometry]].

==Life==
Kostrikin graduated from the [[MSU Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics|Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics]] at [[Moscow State University]] in 1952. In 1960, he earned a [[Doctor of Sciences]] degree under [[Igor Shafarevich]] at the [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]] with a thesis on the [[Burnside problem]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=106010}}</ref> He became a faculty member at Moscow State University in 1963.<ref name=mt/>

==Prizes==
Kostrikin was awarded the [[USSR State Prize]] in 1968 for his research on [[finite groups]] and [[Lie algebra]]s and was elected the corresponding member of the [[USSR Academy of Sciences]] in 1976.<ref name=mt>{{MacTutor|id=Kostrikin|title=Aleksei Ivanovich Kostrikin}}</ref>

==Books==
Alexei Kostrikin published many scientific articles, books and textbooks, including a university textbook about [[algebra]] ''Introduction to algebra'', translated into [[English language|English]] and other languages.
